summary.name: Recipe (Wikipedia article)
summary.one_liner: A Wikipedia article describing what a recipe is, the history of recipes and recipe books from ancient cuneiform tablets to modern cookery writing, and related copyright and components.
use_cases: learning how a recipe is structured
tracing early cookbooks and medical remedy books
summary.what_it_does: The page defines a recipe as a set of instructions listing ingredients and steps, and explains sub-recipes. It traces recipe history from the earliest known cuneiform recipes (1730 BC) through classical, medieval, and early modern cookbooks, including the link between culinary and medical recipes. It describes the modern cookery writing of Eliza Acton and Isabella Beeton, the rise of TV cooking shows and early internet recipe groups. It also lists typical components of a modern recipe and notes that recipes are public domain under U.S. law while cookbook collections can be copyrighted.
notable: Covers recipe history from ancient Mesopotamia to modern cookbooks
Explains the historical link between medical remedies and culinary recipes
Describes typical recipe components and formats
Summarises U.S. copyright status of recipes versus cookbooks
caveats: This is an encyclopedia article, not a recipe management tool; the listing's 'recipe management' label does not match the page content
Copyright notes refer to U.S. law only
